# UI TSX primitives, hooks and signals

Everything a game imports from `@origingame/engine/ui` when authoring custom TSX screens and HUDs (built-in components live in `og api show components --guide`, design tokens and pack slots in `og api show theme-tokens`).

## 1. Host primitives

Compiled away by `nsh-jsx` into host UI ops; every primitive accepts all `HostProps` (§5) plus its own props below.

- **`View`**: `(props: HostProps) => UiNode`
- **`Text`**: `(props: HostProps & { ruby?: string | undefined }) => UiNode`
  A paragraph: its strings, the `<Text>` spans nested in it and the `<Icon>` and `<Image>` in it are laid out as one text, wrapping and aligning together. A span draws in its own classes' size, weight, slant, family, colour and decoration; an icon or image is an inline box its px size (an em square without one), centred on the text's middle. A span with `onPress` is pressed on its glyphs (a link). `select-text` lets the player select it and copy. `ruby` on a span is its annotation (furigana), drawn at half its size centred over it; its line grows to hold it.
- **`Image`**: `(props: HostProps & { src?: Texture | 0 | undefined }) => UiNode`
  A texture (`og.load.texture`; 0 none) drawn over its box, stretched; a class's `nine-<name>` slices a pack's.
- **`Icon`**: `(props: HostProps & { name?: string | undefined }) => UiNode`
- **`Scroll`**: `(props: HostProps) => UiNode`
- **`Line`**: `(props: HostProps & { points: readonly number[]; closed?: boolean | undefined; viewBox?: readonly [number, number] | string | undefined; fit?: "fill" | "contain" | undefined }) => UiNode`
  A polyline in its box: `points` are x, y pairs in CSS px from the box's top left, stroked by `stroke-*` classes (colour and width; the ink and 1 px without), round joins and caps, `closed` back to the first point. With `viewBox` (`[w, h]`, or SVG's `"x y w h"`) the points are in that space, mapped onto the laid-out box as it paints: stretched to fill it, or with `fit="contain"` scaled uniformly and centred; the stroke stays in px. No fill, curves or dashes: what can be an image is an `Image`.
- **`Particles`**: `(props: HostProps & { emitter?: ParticleEmitter | 0 | undefined; seed?: number | undefined; delay?: number | undefined; restart?: string | number | undefined }) => UiNode`
  An engine particle emitter drawn in the UI: `emitter` is an `og.load.emitter` handle (0 none), the same `type particles` asset `og.ParticleSystem` runs in the world. It sits at the centre of the laid-out box, 1 unit a CSS px and +y up (`gravity 0 -600 0` falls down the screen); a `box` shape is the box itself. It starts when the node first draws, `delay` seconds later when given, and again whenever `restart` changes; `seed` and the tick it started are its randomness. Its particles are the node's ink (`text-<colour>`) times the emitter's colour, in painter's order where the node stands, clipped as it is; reduced motion draws none. What needs the scene (fields, collision, light, trails, meshes) does not draw.
- **`Input`**: `(props: HostProps & { value?: string | undefined; placeholder?: string | undefined; type?: "text" | "password" | "number" | "email" | "url" | "tel" | "search" | undefined; inputMode?: "none" | "text" | "decimal" | "numeric" | "tel" | "search" | "email" | "url" | undefined; autoComplete?: string | undefined; secret?: boolean | undefined; multiline?: boolean | undefined; rows?: number | undefined; maxLength?: number | undefined; readOnly?: boolean | undefined; }) => UiNode`

## 2. Control flow, styling and mounting

- **`Show<T>(props: { when: T | undefined | null | false; fallback?: UiChild; keyed?: boolean; children: UiChild | ((value: () => NonNullable<T>) => UiChild) }): UiChild`**
  `<Show when={c} fallback={…} keyed>`: compiled to the renderer's `cond`.
- **`For<T>(props: { each: readonly T[] | undefined | null; key?: (item: T) => unknown; children: (item: () => T, index: () => number) => UiChild }): UiChild`**
  `<For each={items} key={(i) => i.slot}>{(item, index) => …}</For>`: compiled to the renderer's `each`. A row is kept while its key is; without `key`, an object item's `id` is its key (a keyed collection keeps its rows, its entrances and its state, when the view model makes the array afresh), and any other item is its own.
- **`Switch(props: { fallback?: UiChild; children: UiChild }): UiChild`**
  `<Switch fallback={…}><Match when={a}>…</Match><Match when={b}>…</Match></Switch>`: the first case whose `when` holds, made again only when which case holds changes; `fallback` when none does.
- **`Match<T>(props: MatchProps<T>): UiChild`**
  One case of a `Switch`: shown when `when` is truthy and no case before it is.
- **`ErrorBoundary(props: { fallback: UiChild | ((error: unknown, reset: () => void) => UiChild); children: UiChild }): UiChild`**
  Catches synchronous errors thrown while rendering its subtree and renders `fallback` instead, passing the thrown error and a `reset` callback that retries rendering `children`.
- **`packClass(component: string, slot: string, variant?: string | undefined): string`**
  The pack's classes for a component's slot (and its variant): put it last in the slot's `class`. It answers a `@Component.slot[.variant]` token that the UI's class resolver replaces with the pack's strings; the cook folds a call with literal arguments into the strings themselves.
- **`type UiLayer`** = `"hud" | "menu" | "modal" | "popover" | "toast" | "tooltip" | "system"`
  The UI layers a mount may be on.
- **`mount<P>(world: World, Component: (props: P) => UiChild, props: P, options?: { layer?: UiLayer }): () => void`**
  Puts `Component(props)` on `world`'s UI, on `layer` (`hud` without one), and sends it at once, so it builds while the game loads. Returns the unmount.
- **`useWorld(): World`**
  The world of the mount being built or run.
- **`useClock(): Accessor<{ tick: number; dt: number }>`**
  The world's tick and its length in seconds (`dt`), as of the last tick boundary: what a component paces itself by (a typewriter's characters per second), never the wall clock. Read inside a mount.
- **`useStore<T>(store: { subscribe(run: (value: T) => void): () => void }): Accessor<T>`**
  A store as a signal accessor, subscribed while the component lives.

## 3. Localization and formatting

Reactive helpers read inside a mounted component; they re-run automatically when the world's active locale changes.

- **`t(key: string, params?: Record<string, unknown>): string`**
  The translation of `key` in the mount's locale (`params` fill its slots); redrawn when the locale changes.
- **`formatNumber(value: number, format?: unknown): string`**
- **`formatCompact(value: number, decimals?: number): string`**
- **`formatDuration(seconds: number, style?: string): string`**
- **`formatCurrency(amount: number, currency: string): string`**

## 4. Signals and context

Fine-grained Solid-style reactive primitives.

- **`createSignal<T>(value: T, options?: { equals?: false | ((a: T, b: T) => boolean) }): Signal<T>`**
  A value that is written: `count()` reads it, `count.set(n)` writes it.
- **`createMemo<T>(fn: (prev: T | undefined) => T, initial?: T, options?: { equals?: false | ((a: T, b: T) => boolean) }): Accessor<T>`**
  A value computed from others, cached until one of them changes.
- **`createEffect<T>(fn: (prev: T | undefined) => T, initial?: T): void`**
  Runs `fn` after the render effects, and again whenever what it read changes.
- **`createRenderEffect<T>(fn: (prev: T | undefined) => T, initial?: T): void`**
  Runs `fn` now and again whenever what it read changes, before effects.
- **`batch<T>(fn: () => T): T`**
  Writes inside `fn` notify once, when it returns.
- **`untrack<T>(fn: () => T): T`**
  Reads without subscribing.
- **`createRoot<T>(fn: (dispose: () => void) => T): T`**
  An owner nothing disposes but the `dispose` it is handed.
- **`onCleanup(fn: () => void): void`**
  Runs `fn` when the current owner is disposed or runs again.
- **`createContext<T>(defaultValue: T): Context<T>`**
- **`useContext<T>(context: Context<T>): T`**
- **`provide<T, R>(context: Context<T>, value: T, fn: () => R): R`**
  Runs `fn` with `context` set to `value` for everything made under it.
- **`type Accessor<T>`** = `() => T`
  Reads a value and, inside a computation, subscribes it.

### `Signal<T>` (extends `Accessor<T>`)

A written value: read it by calling it, write it with `set`.

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `set` | `(value: T) => void` |  |
| `update` | `(fn: (value: T) => T) => void` |  |

### `Context<T>`

A value components below a provider read with `useContext`.

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `symbol` |  |
| `defaultValue` | `T` |  |

## 5. HostProps

### `HostProps`

What every host element takes. Every optional prop also takes `undefined`.

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `class?` | `string \| undefined` |  |
| `material?` | `UiMaterialBinding \| undefined` |  |
| `classList?` | `Record<string, boolean \| undefined> \| undefined` |  |
| `style?` | `string \| Record<string, string \| number \| undefined> \| undefined` |  |
| `ref?` | `((node: UiNode) => void) \| { set(node: UiNode): void } \| undefined` |  |
| `children?` | `UiChild` |  |
| `onPress?` | `Handler` |  |
| `onTap?` | `Handler` |  |
| `onPointerDown?` | `Handler` |  |
| `onPointerMove?` | `Handler` |  |
| `onPointerUp?` | `Handler` |  |
| `onWheel?` | `Handler` |  |
| `onFocus?` | `Handler` |  |
| `onBlur?` | `Handler` |  |
| `onKey?` | `Handler` |  |
| `onChange?` | `Handler` |  |
| `onLongPress?` | `Handler` | A finger held still on it for 0.5 s; its release then presses nothing. `value` is its box. |
| `onHold?` | `Handler` | A held press, with `hold` set: its progress each frame in `value`, 0 to 1 when it completes; "0" when it lets go early. |
| `hold?` | `number \| undefined` | How long a press must be held for `onHold` to complete, in seconds. |
| `autofocus?` | `boolean \| undefined` | Takes focus when it appears (a dialog's first control). |
| `focusGroup?` | `"stop" \| "wrap" \| undefined` | Its focusable descendants are one group for the arrows and the d-pad: they move among its members first; at its edge `"stop"` leaves it for the control beyond, `"wrap"` goes round inside it. |
| `focusMemory?` | `boolean \| undefined` | With `focusGroup`: focus coming back into it lands on the member it last had. |
| `focusRoving?` | `boolean \| undefined` | With `focusGroup`: the group is one Tab stop (a tab list, a radio group, a toolbar). Tab enters it at its focused member, else its selected, checked or pressed one, else the one it last had, else its first; the arrows move among them all. |
| `draggable?` | `string \| undefined` | Makes it draggable, carrying this data: a press moved past the slop picks it up, as do Enter, Space or `confirm` on it when focused. |
| `dropTarget?` | `string \| undefined` | Makes it a drop target with this id: a carried node let go over it, or put down while it has the focus, drops here. While a node is carried by the keys, targets are focus stops. |
| `onDragStart?` | `Handler` | It was picked up: `key` its `draggable` data, `value` its box. |
| `onDragMove?` | `Handler` | It moved while carried: `key` its data, `value` the `dropTarget` under it (or focused), "" over none. |
| `onDragEnd?` | `Handler` | It was put down: `key` its data, `value` the target's id, "" when cancelled (Escape, `back`, or let go over no target). |
| `onDrop?` | `Handler` | A carried node was dropped on this target: `key` that node's data, `value` this target's box. |
| `onPinch?` | `Handler` | Two fingers that went down on it pinch: `key` is "start", "move" or "end", `value` the scale since they began, x and y their midpoint. |
| `onRotate?` | `Handler` | Two fingers that went down on it turn: as `onPinch`, `value` the turn since they began in radians, clockwise on screen. |
| `onSwipe?` | `Handler` | A pointer that went down on it was let go moving fast (300 px/s, 10 px): `key` its way, "left", "right", "up" or "down"; `value` its velocity, "vx vy" in px/s. A pinch's fingers swipe nothing. |
| `onContextMenu?` | `Handler` | A context menu was asked for on it: the secondary button (a right click) went down over it, at `x`, `y`; or Shift+F10 or the Menu key was pressed with the focus in it, `value` `"key"` and `x`, `y` its box's bottom start. |
| `onScroll?` | `Handler` | Its scroll moved (a `Scroll`), once a frame: `x`, `y` the offset, `value` `"viewportWidth viewportHeight contentWidth contentHeight"`. |
| `scrollbar?` | `boolean \| undefined` | A `Scroll`'s own bar (`Scrollbar.track`, `Scrollbar.thumb`): its thumb follows the scroll and drags it; `false` hides it. Default true. |
| `touchStick?` | `string \| undefined` | An on-screen stick: its box feeds this input action's x and y (from its centre, y up), with no handler. Like `touchPad` and `touchButton`, it is `active:` while a touch holds it. |
| `floatingStick?` | `boolean \| undefined` | Centre a `touchStick` where its finger lands. Its box remains the activation zone. |
| `touchLook?` | `string \| undefined` | A look pad: feed this action the drag since the last fixed tick in CSS px (x right, y up), not a stick deflection. Holding still reads zero. |
| `touchPad?` | `string \| undefined` | An on-screen d-pad: its box feeds this input action, the nearest of eight directions. Held, it carries the way it reads as `data-dir-up`, `data-dir-right`, `data-dir-down` and `data-dir-left` (two on a diagonal), so a class lights the pressed arm (`group-data-dir-up/pad:`). |
| `touchButton?` | `string \| undefined` | An on-screen button: its box presses this input action while a touch that started on it is held. |
| `deadZone?` | `number \| undefined` | A `touchStick`'s dead zone, a ratio of its radius from 0 to 0.95; 0 is the default 0.15. |
| `knob?` | `boolean \| undefined` | Inside a `touchStick`: it moves with the stick's knob as og-input reads it. |
| `onAction?` | `Record<string, Handler> \| undefined` | Input actions handled where focus is (`{ confirm, details }`); the event's `key` names the action. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean \| undefined` |  |
| `tabIndex?` | `number \| undefined` |  |
| `glyph?` | `string \| undefined` | The binding glyph of this input action (a Text's content): the pack's icon for it on the last-used device, an ink mask one em square, else its name (`E`, `LB`). |
| `sound?` | `"open" \| "close" \| "error" \| "reward" \| "toggle" \| "tab" \| "levelup" \| "purchase" \| "countdown" \| "tick" \| "step" \| "swipe" \| "notify" \| "unlock" \| undefined` | The pack event this node sounds when it first paints, once: the sound its pack slot has for it (the slot `packClass` names in its class), else the pack's own, and none when the pack has neither; an event the pack has no clip for sounds the nearest it has (toggle and tab: select, purchase: confirm, levelup and unlock: reward, countdown: press, tick, step and swipe: select, notify: open). These are the events no input fires; a control's hover, press, select, confirm, cancel and back sound by themselves. |
| `exitSound?` | `"open" \| "close" \| "error" \| "reward" \| "toggle" \| "tab" \| "levelup" \| "purchase" \| "countdown" \| "tick" \| "step" \| "swipe" \| "notify" \| "unlock" \| undefined` | The pack sound event played once when this node is removed from the tree (for example `"close"` on a dialog, sheet, popover or menu). |
| `haptic?` | `"tick" \| "tap" \| "thud" \| "double" \| "buzz" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "error" \| "none" \| undefined` | Haptic preset played when this node fires a non-hover interaction or sound cue (`"none"` silences the pack/default haptic). |
| `role?` | `string \| undefined` | crates/og-ui-next/CONVENTIONS.md §Accessibility. |
| `label?` | `string \| undefined` |  |

| `expanded?` | `boolean \| undefined` |  |
| `busy?` | `boolean \| undefined` |  |
| `invalid?` | `boolean \| undefined` | Its value fails the game's checks: screen readers say invalid, and `aria-invalid:` classes apply. |
| `current?` | `boolean \| undefined` |  |
| `hidden?` | `boolean \| undefined` |  |
| `modal?` | `boolean \| undefined` |  |
| `level?` | `number \| undefined` |  |
| `live?` | `"polite" \| "assertive" \| "off" \| undefined` |  |

| `valueMax?` | `number \| undefined` |  |
| `valueNow?` | `number \| undefined` |  |
| `valueText?` | `string \| undefined` |  |
| `wipe?` | `number \| undefined` | The radial wipe of the box's image (an `Image`'s `src`, or a pack's `nine-<name>` class): the share shown, 0 to 1 (1 whole), bound per tick; from `wipeStart` radians (0 up), clockwise unless `wipeCcw`. |
| `wipeStart?` | `number \| undefined` |  |
| `wipeCcw?` | `boolean \| undefined` |  |
| `anchor?` | `Entity \| readonly [number, number, number] \| string \| null \| undefined` | Sits on an entity or a world point `[x, y, z]` instead of in its parent's flow: its box's top left at that point as the tick's camera sees it, at its laid-out size (move it with `translate-*` classes, such as `-translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-full` to stand over it). Off the screen, behind the camera or on a dead entity it is hidden (unless `clamp`): it paints nothing, takes no press and leaves the accessibility tree. Never seen by the simulation. A string anchors it to the UI node of that `name` instead: its top left at that node's laid-out box's top left, `lift`'s x and y fractions of that box's size (`lift={[0, 1, 0]}` stands under it), following it every frame; hidden while no node of that name shows. `occlusion`, `declutter` and `clamp` are for world anchors. |
| `lift?` | `readonly [number, number, number] \| undefined` | The anchor's offset in world units, such as `[0, 2, 0]` over a head. |
| `occlusion?` | `"none" \| "fade" \| "hide" \| undefined` | Behind a drawn mesh, as the tick's camera sees the anchor's point (other than its own entity's): `fade` draws it at 0.35 opacity, `hide` hides it; it carries `data-occluded` either way. Checked at each tick's end. |
| `declutter?` | `"none" \| "stack" \| "hide" \| undefined` | Over another anchored element that declutters: `stack` moves it straight up clear of it, `hide` hides it. Higher `priority`, then the nearer, keeps its place. |
| `priority?` | `number \| undefined` | Which of two decluttering anchors keeps its place: higher first (0). |
| `clamp?` | `"none" \| "edge" \| undefined` | `edge`: off the screen or behind the camera it stays, pinned `clampMargin` px (24) inside the screen's edge toward its point, and carries `data-clamped` and `data-edge-top\|right\|bottom\|left`. Anchored to a UI node (a tooltip, a popover), its drawn box shifts along each axis to stay `clampMargin` px inside the screen. |
| `clampMargin?` | `number \| undefined` |  |
| `scaleAt?` | `number \| undefined` | World distance (in world units) at which the anchored element draws at 1× scale; 0 disables distance scaling. |
| `scaleMin?` | `number \| undefined` | Lower clamp for distance scaling when `scaleAt > 0` (default 0.5). |
| `scaleMax?` | `number \| undefined` | Upper clamp for distance scaling when `scaleAt > 0` (default 1.5). |
| `maxDistance?` | `number \| undefined` | Hide the anchored element beyond this distance along the view axis in world units (0: unlimited). |
| `lod?` | `readonly [number, number] \| string \| undefined` | Distance thresholds `[near, far]` in world units: sets `data-lod-near`, `data-lod-mid`, or `data-lod-far` on the anchored element. |
| `name?` | `string \| undefined` | What `anchor` and `spotlight` find it by. Of the live nodes that share a name, the last made answers. An `Icon`'s `name` is its icon: name a `View` around it. |
| `spotlight?` | `string \| undefined` | A tutorial's spotlight: the `name` of the node it lights. Its own `bg-*` covers the whole surface outside that node's box, and it takes every press there (whether it listens or not: nothing under it gets one), so the lit node keeps its own presses. Its children paint as laid out. While no node of that name shows, it is an ordinary box. It carries `data-lit` while its node shows (`data-lit:bg-scrim`, and `group-data-lit/<g>:hidden` for a fallback without a target). |
| ``[data: `data-${string}`]`` | `string \| number \| boolean \| undefined` | `data-*` states class variants read (`data-ready:`). |

### `UiMaterialBinding`

A loaded custom material over this node and its children, after filters and before mask/opacity.

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `shader` | `UiMaterial` |  |
| `params?` | `Readonly<Record<string, number \| readonly number[]>> \| undefined` | Named finite scalars/vectors. Omitted parameters follow the asset's tuned defaults. |

## 6. UiEvent and node types

### `UiNode`

A node the renderer made: a handle on the UI tree's node `id`.

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `number` |  |

- **`type UiChild`** = `UiNode | string | number | boolean | null | undefined | UiChild[] | (() => UiChild)`
  What a child expression may give: nodes, text, nothing, lists and functions of them.

### `UiEvent`

What an event handler is given.

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `world` | `World` | The world the UI belongs to, for writing intents and commands. |
| `type` | `string` |  |
| `x` | `number` | The pointer on the UI's surface (`onWheel`: the wheel's deltas). |
| `y` | `number` |  |
| `key` | `string` | A key's name (`onKey`) or the input action (`onAction`). |
| `value` | `string` | A control's new value (`onChange`); a hold's progress, 0 to 1, "0" when let go early (`onHold`); the box of the node that hears a pointer event on the surface, `"x y width height"` (`onPointerDown`/`Move`/`Up`, `onLongPress`), so a slider maps `(x - box.x) / box.width`; `"2"` on a double press's second `onPress`. |
